rv.q: “As You Like It” is a rollicking good time, and a wonderfully lighthearted show.

This brainchild from director Daryl Cloran and Vancouver's Bard on the Beach Festival is a taste of honey: the first absolutely must-see show of the season, a production that really needs to move to Broadway after its run so that its genius and infectious exuberance can play to a larger audience.
This is an event that really should not be missed.
The brilliant pairing, centuries in the making, is a poetic explosion of joy and words.
The result is quite simply ecstasy on Navy Pier!
Stellar performances and a standout score make As You Like It a performance you do not want to miss.

The production is the first to arrive on a Chicago Shakespeare Theater stage since the start of the pandemic, and it easily woos its happily returning live audience by way of an ingenious riff on a classic.

Yet in Chicago Shakespeare Theater's wacky take on "As You Like It," a stellar company, everybody from actors to designers and I dare say set painters, has created an irresistible winner that deserves to pack 'em in, well, "Eight Days a Week."
The highest compliment we can deliver to this version of As It is that it works.
Most of the songs suit the story, which mostly adheres to Shakespeare's original, with one exception (more about that later).
The songs slot into the action well, and are often surprisingly spot on.

I’ll admit, I had my doubts, but amazingly this coupling really does work, with some songs providing spot-on commentary on the plot, replacing existing tunes and poetry from the play, and others bringing new meaning and perspectives.
This is a marvelous way to bring Shakespeare to people who do not enjoy ( or understand) the works of the master.
In the end, the production’s overarching concept just didn’t draw me in.
